subject: Throughput certification and reserved commit path for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nimbushealth.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Reed <m.reed@nimbushealth.com>, Ops Team <ops@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput goals and reserved commit question

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the proposal. A few follow-ups from our side before we share this with procurement: we need clarity on the measurable acceptance criteria for the Dedicated GPU pool. Specifically: tokens/sec vs requests/sec (which metric you recommend for a chat-heavy workload), how latency SLOs factor into crediting, and the exact test harness you use for certification.

We're also trying to understand how commit bands map to discounts — our initial target is 1.5B tokens/month steady-state, but we have spikes to 7–8k concurrent requests during peak hours. Will Redwood size a pool with headroom or do we rely on autoscale?

Can you share an example test script or the CSV report format so we can run a shadow test in our staging VPC?

Thanks,
Laura
VP Platform Engineering
Nimbus Health
From: rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput goals and reserved commit question

Laura — thanks for the thoughtful questions. Long answer short: we certify Dedicated throughput on both tokens/sec (for cost-accounting) and requests/sec (for concurrency/latency), with a single acceptance run that maps to both guarantees. High-level notes below; attaching the test harness and an example CSV export for the measurement run.

- Measurement approach: we run a 3-hour acceptance window (can be shortened to 60m for negotiated cases) that reproduces your traffic mix (prompt lengths, completion lengths, function-calls). The run reports: sustained tokens/sec (95th percentile over 30-min sliding windows), peak requests/sec (99th percentile), and tail latency (99.9th pct for generation time per request).
- Pass criteria: sustained tokens/sec >= committed_band * 0.95, peak requests/sec >= declared concurrency * 0.9, and 99.9th latency < agreed SLO (default 800ms for 8k concurrent requests at 512 token sequence). Failures trigger prorated credits by the shortfall bucket.
- Pool sizing: we propose a baseline GPU pool sized for your steady-state (1.5B tokens/mo) with a reserved burst tranche for peak hours. Autoscale is available but not guaranteed for commit-backed pricing — committed pools are sized and pinned to ensure predictability.
- Discount tiers: commit bands (bronze/silver/gold) map to stepped discounts; deeper discounts available for multi-quarter commitments and for larger headroom commitments.

Attached: throughput-test-script.py (example harness), nh-throughput-report-20270621.csv (sample run). I'll loop Ben and Marissa in for commercial and operational specifics.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nimbushealth.com>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Jun 2027 09:26:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput goals and reserved commit question

Laura — hi from Ben. A few commercial details to make this concrete:

1) Commit and discount mapping (example):
   - Band A (1.0B–2.0B tokens/mo): 18% list discount, baseline pool sized to 1.5B, one reserved burst tranche (20% capacity) for peak hour routing.
   - Band B (2.0B–4.0B tokens/mo): 26% list discount, baseline pool sized to 2.75B, two reserved burst tranches (20% + 10%).
   - Band C (4.0B+ tokens/mo): 32% list discount, custom pool + priority capacity.

2) Measurement and credits: if sustained tokens/sec during the agreed run is below the 95% threshold, we apply a sliding credit as follows: 95–90% = 10% credit on monthly committed fees, 89–80% = 25% credit, <80% = 50% credit. This is in addition to remediation options (hotfix routing, extra capacity for the test period).

3) Latency carve-outs: for generation-heavy requests with >1024 token windows, we suggest a separate latency tier in the SOW (higher cost, higher headroom); otherwise the default 99.9th latency SLO will be 800ms at the declared concurrency.

4) Test run logistics: we can run the acceptance test in your staging VPC (preferred) or our private test harness accessing a snapshot of your model weights (requires additional NDAs). Typical timeline is 5 business days from SOW signature to test run.

If this aligns, Marissa will draft an SOW and we can attach the DocuSign link. Happy to tighten the credit buckets if procurement pushes back.

—Ben
Director, Commercial Strategy — Redwood Inference
From: Laura Chen <laura.chen@nimbushealth.com>
To: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, rachel_kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Reed <m.reed@nimbushealth.com>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Jun 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput goals and reserved commit question

Thanks Ben/Rachel — this is very helpful. A couple of quick clarifications so my procurement and SRE team can move forward:

- We prefer the staging VPC test run. Can you send a checklist of network and IAM requirements so our infra team can provision?
- The 3-hour acceptance window is fine; procurement will push for the 60-minute negotiated test if we can prove representative traffic ahead of time. Is there a lightweight smoke harness we can run that would be admissible?
- For credits: procurement wants a cap on total credits (so the vendor is protected). Would Redwood accept a 3x cap (credits not to exceed 3x monthly committed fee)?

If you can add those items to the SOW draft (network checklist, optional 60m test path, credit cap language), we should be able to circulate and sign next week.

I'll also schedule a short call with our SRE (Marcus) and your ops lead to walk the checklist.

Regards,
Laura
VP Platform Engineering — Nimbus Health
